Privacy and credits

On this page
  • Privacy in short
  • The About page
  • Credits

Privacy in short

Taqwim has no accounts, no ads, no analytics and no tracking. It collects, sells and shares no personal data.

  • On your device only: your settings, your location and saved places, the mosques you add, your sounds and the map areas you download. Deleting the app deletes them.
  • Your location comes from the device's GPS or from a place you pick. It is used on the device to compute the prayer times, the Qibla and the sky, and is never sent anywhere. The compass and motion sensors are used the same way. Prayer alerts are scheduled on the device.
  • When Taqwim goes online:
    • to show a street map, download a map area, or read the street data for the nearby mosques and directions, it loads map tiles from OpenFreeMap, and from EOX for the satellite layer when you turn it on. Like any website, these servers see your device's internet address and the part of the map loaded, nothing else;
    • when you tap Open in Google Maps or Open in Waze, that app receives the mosque's position, and its own privacy policy applies.
  • Backups: Back up settings writes a file that you keep. Your device's own backup (Google or iCloud) may also keep the settings file in your account if you have it on.
  • Permissions: location, notifications, exact alarms (Android) and playing the Athan in the background. Taqwim works without any of them; you then choose your place by hand.

Read the full privacy policy.

The About page

In the app, open Settings → General → About Taqwim. It shows:

  • the app's version;
  • the credit for the Athan recording;
  • a summary of the privacy policy;
  • the sources of the data, maps and calculations, with their licences;
  • the open-source software Taqwim is built with, and the full licence texts that must accompany it.

Credits

The Athan

The built-in Athan is in the voice of Sheikh Abdullah Al-Zaylai, Al-Rajhi Mosque, Abha. The About page names the source of the recording, and the recording is removed from the app at the request of the Sheikh or of the recording's maker.

Data and maps

  • GeoNames: the cities, countries and their names (CC BY 4.0).
  • Wikidata: everyday place names in Arabic and English (public domain).
  • OpenStreetMap, through OpenFreeMap: the street maps and the nearby mosques (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL).
  • Sentinel-2 cloudless by EOX: the satellite layer of the Qibla map (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
  • Natural Earth: the built-in world map (public domain).
  • IANA Time Zone Database: the first guess of your location from the device's time zone (public domain).
  • NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio: the Moon photo on the Phases page (public domain).
  • Yale Bright Star Catalogue (NASA HEASARC) and ConstellationLines: the stars and constellations of the sky sphere.
  • World Magnetic Model WMM2025 (NOAA NCEI and BGS): the magnetic declination (public domain).

Calculations

  • Astronomy Engine by Don Cross: the Sun, Moon and planet calculations, ported to Rust (MIT licence).
  • Odeh (2004) and Yallop (1997): the crescent visibility criteria.
  • Espenak and Meeus; Morrison and Stephenson (2004): the difference between clock and astronomical time, and its uncertainty for historical dates.
  • Laskar (1986); Chapront-Touzé and Chapront (1988): the mean lengths of the year and the lunar month in the Astronomical Calculator.

The full list, with every software library and its licence, is on the About page.
